import HepLean.Lorentz.Group.Proper
import HepLean.Lorentz.RealVector.NormOne
/-!
# Boosts

This file defines those Lorentz which are boosts.

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking
a four velocity `u` to a four velocity `v`.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = stdBasis 0`.

## References

- The main argument follows: Guillem Cobos, The Lorentz Group, 2015:
  https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/bitstream/2445/68763/2/memoria.pdf

-/
noncomputable section

namespace LorentzGroup

open Lorentz.Contr.NormOne
open Lorentz
open TensorProduct

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₁ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ) • v.1.1
  map_add' x y := by
    simp [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, tmul_add, add_tmul, mul_add, add_smul]
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,
      Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V, CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse,
      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,
      smul_tmul, tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_comm 2 c, mul_assoc, mul_smul]

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₂ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  map_add' x y := by
    simp only
    rw [← add_smul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    field_simp [add_tmul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    ring
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [smul_tmul, tmul_smul]
    rw [map_smul]
    conv =>
      lhs; lhs; rhs; lhs
      change (c * (contrContrContractField (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (u.val.val + v.val.val))))
    rw [mul_div_assoc, neg_mul_eq_mul_neg, smul_smul]
    rfl

lemma genBoostAux₂_self (u : FuturePointing d) : genBoostAux₂ u u = - genBoostAux₁ u u := by
  ext1 x
  simp only [genBoostAux₂, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, genBoostAux₁, LinearMap.neg_apply]
  rw [neg_smul]
  apply congrArg
  conv => lhs; rhs; rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  rw [smul_smul]
  congr 1
  rw [u.1.2]
  conv => lhs; lhs; rhs; rhs; change 1
  rw [show 1 + (1 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) by ring]
  simp only [isUnit_iff_ne_zero, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true,
    IsUnit.div_mul_cancel]
  rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  simp only [tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]

/-- An generalised boost. This is a Lorentz transformation which takes the four velocity `u`
to `v`. -/
def genBoost (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d :=
  LinearMap.id + genBoostAux₁ u v + genBoostAux₂ u v

lemma genBoost_mul_one_plus_contr (u v : FuturePointing d) (x : Contr d) :
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • genBoost u v x =
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • x +

  simp only [genBoost, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, id_eq]

    (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • v.1.1
    + (- ⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  · congr 1
    · congr 1
      rw [genBoostAux₁]
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr 1
      ring
    · rw [genBoostAux₂]
      simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V, Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V,
        CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse, Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor,
        Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj, neg_smul, LinearMap.coe_mk,
        AddHom.coe_mk, smul_neg]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr
      have h1 := FuturePointing.one_add_metric_non_zero u v
      field_simp

namespace genBoost

/--
  This lemma states that for a given four-velocity `u`, the general boost
  transformation `genBoost u u` is equal to the identity linear map `LinearMap.id`.
-/
lemma self (u : FuturePointing d) : genBoost u u = LinearMap.id := by
  ext x
  simp only [genBoost, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.id_coe, id_eq]
  rw [genBoostAux₂_self]
  simp only [LinearMap.neg_apply, add_neg_cancel_right]

/-- A generalised boost as a matrix. -/
def toMatrix (u v : FuturePointing d) : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ :=
  LinearMap.toMatrix ContrMod.stdBasis ContrMod.stdBasis (genBoost u v)

lemma toMatrix_mulVec (u v : FuturePointing d) (x : Contr d) :
    (toMatrix u v) *ᵥ x = genBoost u v x :=
  ContrMod.ext (LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr ContrMod.stdBasis ContrMod.stdBasis (genBoost u v) x)

open minkowskiMatrix in
@[simp]
lemma toMatrix_apply (u v : FuturePointing d) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    (toMatrix u v) μ ν = η μ μ * (⟪ContrMod.stdBasis μ, ContrMod.stdBasis ν⟫ₘ + 2 *
    ⟪ContrMod.stdBasis ν, u.val.val⟫ₘ * ⟪ContrMod.stdBasis μ, v.val.val⟫ₘ
    - ⟪ContrMod.stdBasis μ, u.val.val + v.val.val⟫ₘ *
    ⟪ContrMod.stdBasis ν, u.val.val + v.val.val⟫ₘ /
    (1 + ⟪u.val.val, v.val.val⟫ₘ)) := by
  rw [contrContrContractField.matrix_apply_stdBasis (Λ := toMatrix u v) μ ν, toMatrix_mulVec]
  simp only [genBoost, genBoostAux₁, genBoostAux₂, smul_add, neg_smul, LinearMap.add_apply,
    LinearMap.id_apply, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, contrContrContractField.basis_left,

  ring_nf
  simp only [Pi.add_apply, Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,
    Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V, CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse,
    Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,
    Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.sub_apply, Pi.neg_apply]
  left
  ring

informal_statement: For any future-pointing vectors \( u \), \( v \), and any contravariant vector \( x \), the matrix transformation \( \text{toMatrix}(u, v) \) applied to \( x \) through standard matrix multiplication yields the result of the function \( \text{genBoost}(u, v, x) \).
informal_proof:
To establish the equality \( (\text{toMatrix}\, u\, v) \times x = \text{genBoost}\, u\, v\, x \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Matrix Representation**: Recognize that the matrix \( \text{toMatrix}\, u\, v \) represents a linear transformation defined by \( u \) and \( v \).

2. **Matrix-Vector Multiplication**: The product \( (\text{toMatrix}\, u\, v) \times x \) is equivalent to the linear transformation of \( x \) under this matrix.

3. **Component-wise Equality**: By definition, \( \text{genBoost}\, u\, v\, x \) represents the result of transforming \( x \) under the same transformation.

4. **Extensionality**: Since the equality holds for the standard basis vectors (as per the `ContrMod.ext` axiom), and linear transformations are determined by their action on a basis, the equality holds for all vectors \( x \).

Thus, the matrix transformation applied to \( x \) matches the result of \( \text{genBoost}\, u\, v\, x \).

      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,

def genBoostAux₂ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  map_add' x y := by
    simp only
    rw [← add_smul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    field_simp [add_tmul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    ring
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [smul_tmul, tmul_smul]
    rw [map_smul]
    conv =>
      lhs; lhs; rhs; lhs
      change (c * (contrContrContractField (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (u.val.val + v.val.val))))
    rw [mul_div_assoc, neg_mul_eq_mul_neg, smul_smul]
    rfl

lemma genBoostAux₂_self (u : FuturePointing d) : genBoostAux₂ u u = - genBoostAux₁ u u := by
  ext1 x
  simp only [genBoostAux₂, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, genBoostAux₁, LinearMap.neg_apply]
  rw [neg_smul]
  apply congrArg
  conv => lhs; rhs; rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  rw [smul_smul]
  congr 1
  rw [u.1.2]
  conv => lhs; lhs; rhs; rhs; change 1
  rw [show 1 + (1 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) by ring]
  simp only [isUnit_iff_ne_zero, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true,
    IsUnit.div_mul_cancel]
  rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  simp only [tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]

/-- An generalised boost. This is a Lorentz transformation which takes the four velocity `u`
to `v`. -/
def genBoost (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d :=
  LinearMap.id + genBoostAux₁ u v + genBoostAux₂ u v

lemma genBoost_mul_one_plus_contr (u v : FuturePointing d) (x : Contr d) :
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • genBoost u v x =
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • x +
    (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • v.1.1
    - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1) := by
  simp only [genBoost, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, id_eq]
  rw [smul_add, smul_add]
  trans (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • x +
    (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • v.1.1
    + (- ⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  · congr 1
    · congr 1
      rw [genBoostAux₁]
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr 1
      ring
    · rw [genBoostAux₂]
      simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V, Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V,
        CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse, Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor,
        Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj, neg_smul, LinearMap.coe_mk,
        AddHom.coe_mk, smul_neg]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr
      have h1 := FuturePointing.one_add_metric_non_zero u v
      field_simp
  · rw [neg_smul]
    rfl

First, the `toMatrix` function is designed to convert two `FuturePointing` objects into a matrix representation. This is achieved by applying the `LinearMap.toMatrix` method, which transforms a linear map into a matrix based on the chosen basis vectors—the standard basis in this case.

The `genBoost` function encapsulates the logic for generating the linear transformation that `u` and `v` represent. By applying this function, the `toMatrix` function ensures that the transformation is linear and can be represented as a matrix. The matrix form is beneficial because it allows for easy manipulation, composition of transformations, and simplifies computations that involve these transformations.

In summary, the `toMatrix` function leverages the `genBoost` function to create a matrix that accurately represents the linear transformation defined by the `FuturePointing` objects `u` and `v`. This matrix representation facilitates further operations and analyses that rely on linear algebra principles.

/-!
# Boosts

This file defines those Lorentz which are boosts.

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking
a four velocity `u` to a four velocity `v`.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = stdBasis 0`.

## References

- The main argument follows: Guillem Cobos, The Lorentz Group, 2015:
  https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/bitstream/2445/68763/2/memoria.pdf

  map_add' x y := by
    simp [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, tmul_add, add_tmul, mul_add, add_smul]
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,

      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,

    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    ring

    simp only [smul_tmul, tmul_smul]
    rw [map_smul]
    conv =>

This file defines those Lorentz which are boosts.

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking

# Boosts

This file defines those Lorentz which are boosts.

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking
a four velocity `u` to a four velocity `v`.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = stdBasis 0`.

## References

- The main argument follows: Guillem Cobos, The Lorentz Group, 2015:
  https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/bitstream/2445/68763/2/memoria.pdf

namespace LorentzGroup

open Lorentz.Contr.NormOne
open Lorentz
open TensorProduct

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₁ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ) • v.1.1
  map_add' x y := by
    simp [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, tmul_add, add_tmul, mul_add, add_smul]
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,
      Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V, CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse,
      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,
      smul_tmul, tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_comm 2 c, mul_assoc, mul_smul]

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₂ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  map_add' x y := by
    simp only
    rw [← add_smul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    field_simp [add_tmul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    ring
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [smul_tmul, tmul_smul]
    rw [map_smul]
    conv =>
      lhs; lhs; rhs; lhs
      change (c * (contrContrContractField (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (u.val.val + v.val.val))))
    rw [mul_div_assoc, neg_mul_eq_mul_neg, smul_smul]
    rfl

lemma genBoostAux₂_self (u : FuturePointing d) : genBoostAux₂ u u = - genBoostAux₁ u u := by
  ext1 x
  simp only [genBoostAux₂, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, genBoostAux₁, LinearMap.neg_apply]
  rw [neg_smul]
  apply congrArg
  conv => lhs; rhs; rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  rw [smul_smul]
  congr 1
  rw [u.1.2]
  conv => lhs; lhs; rhs; rhs; change 1
  rw [show 1 + (1 : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) by ring]
  simp only [isUnit_iff_ne_zero, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true,
    IsUnit.div_mul_cancel]
  rw [← (two_smul ℝ u.val.val)]
  simp only [tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]

/-- An generalised boost. This is a Lorentz transformation which takes the four velocity `u`
to `v`. -/
def genBoost (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d :=
  LinearMap.id + genBoostAux₁ u v + genBoostAux₂ u v

lemma genBoost_mul_one_plus_contr (u v : FuturePointing d) (x : Contr d) :
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • genBoost u v x =
    (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • x +
    (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • v.1.1
    - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1) := by
  simp only [genBoost, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, id_eq]
  rw [smul_add, smul_add]
  trans (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • x +
    (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ * (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • v.1.1
    + (- ⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)
  · congr 1
    · congr 1
      rw [genBoostAux₁]
      simp only [LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr 1
      ring
    · rw [genBoostAux₂]
      simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V, Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V,
        CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse, Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor,
        Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj, neg_smul, LinearMap.coe_mk,
        AddHom.coe_mk, smul_neg]
      rw [smul_smul]
      congr
      have h1 := FuturePointing.one_add_metric_non_zero u v
      field_simp
  · rw [neg_smul]
    rfl

  This lemma states that for a given four-velocity `u`, the general boost
  transformation `genBoost u u` is equal to the identity linear map `LinearMap.id`.
-/
lemma self (u : FuturePointing d) : genBoost u u = LinearMap.id := by

rag.name: IsLinearMap
rag.content:
/-- A map `f` between modules over a semiring is linear if it satisfies the two properties
`f (x + y) = f x + f y` and `f (c • x) = c • f x`. The predicate `IsLinearMap R f` asserts this
property. A bundled version is available with `LinearMap`, and should be favored over
`IsLinearMap` most of the time. -/
structure IsLinearMap (R : Type u) {M : Type v} {M₂ : Type w} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M] [Module R M₂] (f : M → M₂) : Prop where
  /-- A linear map preserves addition. -/
  map_add : ∀ x y, f (x + y) = f x + f y
  /-- A linear map preserves scalar multiplication. -/
  map_smul : ∀ (c : R) (x), f (c • x) = c • f x

protected theorem map_smul (f : X →[M'] Y) (m : M') (x : X) : f (m • x) = m • f x :=
  map_smul f m x

To prove the equivalence, we proceed methodically by simplifying each component of both sides of the equation. 

1. **Initial Expression**: Begin with the left-hand side expression `((1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ) • genBoost u v x)` and expand the `genBoost` function using its definition.

This file defines those Lorentz which are boosts.

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking
a four velocity `u` to a four velocity `v`.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = stdBasis 0`.

open TensorProduct

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₁ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ) • v.1.1
  map_add' x y := by
    simp [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, tmul_add, add_tmul, mul_add, add_smul]
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,
      Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V, CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse,
      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,
      smul_tmul, tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_comm 2 c, mul_assoc, mul_smul]

  toFun x := - (⟪x, u.1.1 + v.1.1⟫ₘ / (1 + ⟪u.1.1, v.1.1⟫ₘ)) • (u.1.1 + v.1.1)

    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    field_simp [add_tmul]
    apply congrFun (congrArg _ _)
    ring
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [smul_tmul, tmul_smul]
    rw [map_smul]
    conv =>
      lhs; lhs; rhs; lhs
      change (c * (contrContrContractField (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (u.val.val + v.val.val))))
    rw [mul_div_assoc, neg_mul_eq_mul_neg, smul_smul]

rag.name: IsLinearMap
rag.content:
/-- A map `f` between modules over a semiring is linear if it satisfies the two properties
`f (x + y) = f x + f y` and `f (c • x) = c • f x`. The predicate `IsLinearMap R f` asserts this
property. A bundled version is available with `LinearMap`, and should be favored over
`IsLinearMap` most of the time. -/
structure IsLinearMap (R : Type u) {M : Type v} {M₂ : Type w} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M] [Module R M₂] (f : M → M₂) : Prop where
  /-- A linear map preserves addition. -/
  map_add : ∀ x y, f (x + y) = f x + f y
  /-- A linear map preserves scalar multiplication. -/
  map_smul : ∀ (c : R) (x), f (c • x) = c • f x

rag.name: LinearMap.isLinear
rag.content:
theorem isLinear : IsLinearMap R fₗ :=
  ⟨fₗ.map_add', fₗ.map_smul'⟩

rag.name: LinearMap.semilinearMapClass
rag.content:
instance semilinearMapClass : SemilinearMapClass (M →ₛₗ[σ] M₃) σ M M₃ where
  map_add f := f.map_add'
  map_smulₛₗ := LinearMap.map_smul'

rag.name: LinearMapClass.linearMap
rag.content:
/-- Reinterpret an element of a type of linear maps as a linear map. -/
abbrev linearMap : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂ := SemilinearMapClass.semilinearMap f

rag.name: LinearMap.isLinear
rag.content:
theorem isLinear : IsLinearMap R fₗ :=
  ⟨fₗ.map_add', fₗ.map_smul'⟩

/--
Congruence in the function argument: if `a₁ = a₂` then `f a₁ = f a₂` for
any (nondependent) function `f`. This is more powerful than it might look at first, because
you can also use a lambda expression for `f` to prove that
`<something containing a₁> = <something containing a₂>`. This function is used
internally by tactics like `congr` and `simp` to apply equalities inside
subterms.

For more information: [Equality](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/quantifiers_and_equality.html#equality)
-/
theorem congrArg {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {a₁ a₂ : α} (f : α → β) (h : Eq a₁ a₂) : Eq (f a₁) (f a₂) :=
  h ▸ rfl

We first define generalised boosts, which are restricted lorentz transformations taking
a four velocity `u` to a four velocity `v`.

A boost is the special case of a generalised boost when `u = stdBasis 0`.

## References

- The main argument follows: Guillem Cobos, The Lorentz Group, 2015:
  https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/bitstream/2445/68763/2/memoria.pdf

-/

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- An auxiliary linear map used in the definition of a generalised boost. -/
def genBoostAux₁ (u v : FuturePointing d) : ContrMod d →ₗ[ℝ] ContrMod d where
  toFun x := (2 * ⟪x, u.val.val⟫ₘ) • v.1.1
  map_add' x y := by
    simp [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, tmul_add, add_tmul, mul_add, add_smul]
  map_smul' c x := by
    simp only [Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorObj_V,
      Action.instMonoidalCategory_tensorUnit_V, CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm_inverse,
      Action.functorCategoryEquivalence_functor, Action.FunctorCategoryEquivalence.functor_obj_obj,
      smul_tmul, tmul_smul, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_comm 2 c, mul_assoc, mul_smul]
